topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory welcome, connects the lecture to prior histopathology practicals, and sets out the day's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Viral origins of oncogenes and assays for cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the study of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and how cellular transformation is experimentally assayed in the laboratory.

topics.label: Functional classifications and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the operational categories of cancer mutations and illustrate their dominant, recessive, and dominant-negative genetic mechanisms using cell cycle regulators.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of sequence and chromosomal instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific failures in DNA repair pathways, replication proofreading, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression, hereditary predisposition, and clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how stepwise mutation accumulation drives tumor progression and how inherited mutations or therapeutic pressures influence disease dynamics.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the lecture with an offer to answer questions, suggested reading material, and an outlook on the next lecture.
